title: ZIA restore point limits, golden point and scheduled eviction

prose.text: Restore points are a bounded set with different rules for manual and scheduled creation. Whether a failed scheduled backup is logged or alerted is not stated {{gap:scheduled-failure-logging}}.
Creation: {{manual-or-scheduled}} {{scheduled-access}} {{schedule-fields}} The page that lists them: {{page-columns}} Name and description limits: {{field-limits}}
A Backup & Restore category exists in the audit log filters: [[zia.audit-logs.what-is-recorded]]. What a restore does to the live configuration is in [[zia.backup-restore.restore-semantics]].

checks.do: How many restore points exist, and whether the point you need is the golden one, before a change window.
Whether a scheduled backup is due that would evict the point you need, since the oldest point is removed to make room.

manual-or-scheduled.statement: Backups are created manually on demand or automatically on a schedule in the Admin Console; each restore point records the date and time its backup was created.

quotes: A restore point represents the date and time when a backup was created
Backups can be automated using schedules or created manually on demand in the Zscaler Admin Console.

limit-12.statement: An organization can have up to 12 restore points, counting manual and scheduled backups together.

quotes: An organization can have up to 12 restore points, including manual and scheduled backups.

golden.statement: One restore point can be designated the Golden Restore Point; it exists indefinitely and cannot be deleted, and only one can exist at a time.

quotes: You can designate one of the restore points as the Golden Restore Point that exists indefinitely
The Golden Restore Point cannot be deleted.
There can be only one Golden Restore Point at any given point in time.
There can be only one golden restore point at any given point in time, and you cannot delete it.

manual-blocked-at-limit.statement: At 12 restore points a new restore point cannot be added manually until an existing one is deleted.

quotes: If the number of restore points reaches a limit of 12, you cannot add a new restore point manually without deleting an existing one.
If the number of restore points reaches a limit of 12, you cannot add a new restore point manually without deleting an existing one.

scheduled-evicts.statement: When a scheduled backup would exceed the limit, the oldest restore point is removed to make room; if the oldest is the golden one, the next oldest is removed instead.

quotes: during scheduled automatic backup, the oldest restore point is removed to create the new one when the limit is exceeded.
If the oldest restore point is a Golden Restore Point, then the next oldest restore point is removed.

If the number of restore points reaches a limit of 12, then the next restore point is created by removing the oldest restore point in the list. However, if the oldest restore point is a Golden Restore Point, then the next oldest restore point is removed.

scheduled-access.statement: Scheduled backups must be requested from the Zscaler Account team: the Creating Scheduled Backup Configuration page says to contact the Zscaler Account team to access the feature.

quotes: To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.

schedule-fields.statement: A scheduled backup configuration has a Restore Point Prefix Name, a Frequency of Weekly (with a Day of the week) or Monthly (with a Date), a Restore Point Creation Time and a Time Zone in which the configuration is valid.

quotes: Restore Point Prefix Name: Enter a restore point prefix name.
Frequency: Select either Weekly or Monthly.
Date: Select the date on which you want the restore point to be created. This field appears when the Frequency is selected as Monthly.
Day: Select the day of the week when you want the restore point to be created. This field appears when the Frequency is selected as Weekly.
Restore Point Creation Time: Select the time at which you want the restore point to be created.
Time Zone: Select the time zone in which the scheduled backup configuration should be valid.

page-columns.statement: The Backup & Restore page lists each restore point with Restore Point Name, Description, Created By and Created On, and marks the golden one with a flag icon.

quotes: Restore Point Name: The name of the restore point.
Description: The description of the restore point, if available.
Created By: The admin that created the restore point.
Created On: The date and time the restore point was created.
A restore point with the Flag icon alongside it represents a Golden Restore Point

field-limits.statement: A restore point name is limited to 128 characters and its description to 10,240 bytes.

quotes: | Restore Point Name | 128 characters |
| Restore Point Description | 10,240 bytes |

golden-survives-eviction.statement: A scheduled backup at the limit removes the oldest non-golden restore point without any administrator choosing it, while the Golden Restore Point is never evicted or deleted; designating the point to retain as golden is what protects it.
golden-survives-eviction.conditions: Only one golden point can exist, so only one point can be protected this way.

scheduled-failure-logging.title: Whether a failed scheduled backup is logged or alerted
scheduled-failure-logging.detail: The scheduled backup configuration page describes the fields and the 12-point eviction but does not say whether a failed scheduled backup is logged or raises an alert.
